reason: The only offered action puts the frozen core in a cold workspace to prepare a view.
expectation: I expect the core to be prepared while staying frozen; I do not know exactly how.

effect: The case now has a window and the next goal is to resolve the speck.
reaction: I am curious whether the speck will be recognizable.
reason: The lamp is the only offered combination and should illuminate the window.
expectation: I expect a better lit view of the core, though perhaps not enough detail yet.

effect: Backlighting shows projections and places the speck deep within the band, making a closer look worthwhile.
reaction: The folded outline is intriguing, and its position makes it feel like part of the sample.
reason: The cold microscope is the only offered action and should resolve finer detail without warming the sample.
expectation: I expect a magnified view of the speck, but not necessarily an identification.

effect: The microscope resolves the speck into a body with segmented limbs, a much more specific discovery than the earlier outline.
reaction: Surprised and moved by the quiet pause before the message to Earth; the finding feels momentous.

mostWorthwhile.text: The microscope reveal was most worthwhile: the detail and the narrator's stillness made the long effort to preserve the sample pay off.

leastWorthwhile.text: Opening the case in the preparation enclosure was functional but less engaging on its own; it offered no detail beyond creating a windowed case.

surprise.text: I expected a closer view but not an unmistakable articulated body with folded limbs.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: preparing a window, lighting the ice, and using a cold microscope followed the goal. Each step offered only one gameplay action, so there was little decision-making.

continue.text: Yes. I want to see how Earth responds and what can be learned from the body; the discovery gives me a reason to continue despite the very linear interactions.
